name: noodle soup
ingredients: 2 pak choi or a handful of greens
steps: Simmer the stock with the ginger and garlic for 15 minutes so it takes on flavour, then lift them out.
Cook the noodles separately as the packet says, usually 4 to 6 minutes, and rinse so they do not cloud the broth.
Poach the chicken, tofu or prawns in the broth for 6 to 8 minutes, until cooked through.
Add the greens for the last 2 minutes so they stay bright.
Build the bowl: noodles first, then the protein, then the hot broth. Finish with soy, lime, spring onion and herbs.

name: rice dish
ingredients: 2 carrots or a mix of vegetables
2 tsp of the region’s warm spice mix (cumin, coriander, paprika)
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then soak 20 minutes. This is what keeps the grains separate.
Brown the protein in the oil over high heat for 6 minutes, then set aside.
Cook the onion over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until deep gold, then add garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Return the protein with the stock, cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Drain the rice, stir it in, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Rest 10 minutes off the heat, then fork through and finish with herbs.

name: slow stew
ingredients: 400g meat, or 2 tins of beans or lentils
2 tsp ground spices from the region
steps: Brown the meat in the oil over high heat for 6 to 8 minutes for colour, then lift out. Skip this if using beans.
Cook the onion over medium heat for 10 minutes until properly golden, not just soft.
Add garlic and spices and stir for 1 minute, until they smell toasted rather than raw.
Add tomatoes, carrots, stock and the meat. Bring to the boil, then drop to the lowest simmer.
Cover and cook 45 minutes for meat, or 20 minutes for beans, until everything gives easily.
Season, rest 5 minutes and finish with herbs.

name: grilled dish
ingredients: 500g chicken thighs, lamb or firm vegetables
1 tbsp of the region’s spice blend
steps: Mix the oil, garlic, spices and citrus into a marinade and coat the meat or vegetables.
Leave for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or overnight in the fridge. This is where nearly all the flavour comes from.
Get the grill, griddle or oven properly hot — 220°C, or coals with a white ash.
Cook for 5 to 7 minutes each side for chicken thighs, 3 to 4 for lamb, until charred outside and cooked through with no pink.
Rest for 5 minutes before slicing. Serve with bread or rice, salad and yoghurt.

name: bread or filled dough
ingredients: 200g filling: spiced vegetables, lentils or minced meat
steps: Mix flour, salt, water and 1 tbsp oil into a soft dough and knead for 6 to 8 minutes until smooth and springy.
Cover and rest for 30 minutes. Rested dough rolls thin without tearing.
Cook the onion in the rest of the oil for 8 minutes, add the filling and spices and cook 8 minutes more. Cool before filling.
Divide the dough, roll each piece thin, and fill or leave plain.
Cook in a dry hot pan for 1 to 2 minutes a side until blistered, or bake at 220°C for 12 to 15 minutes until golden.

name: fresh dish
ingredients: 300g very fresh fish suitable for raw preparation, or 2 tins of beans
3 tbsp olive oil or 200ml coconut milk
steps: If using raw fish, buy it from a fishmonger, tell them it is for raw preparation, and keep it cold until the moment you cut it.
Cut the fish into 1.5cm pieces and cover with the lime juice. Chill 15 to 20 minutes, until the outside turns opaque.
Finely dice the cucumber, tomato and onion while it sits.
Drain off most of the lime, then fold everything together with the oil or coconut milk, chilli and herbs.
Season and eat within the hour — this does not keep.

name: staple and sauce
ingredients: 300g of the staple: maize meal, semolina, cassava flour or couscous
steps: Make the sauce first: cook the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, add spices for 1 minute, then tomatoes and 200ml water.
Simmer the sauce for 15 minutes, add the protein and cook 10 to 15 minutes until done through.
Fold the greens in for the last 2 minutes.
For the staple, bring the water to the boil, then rain the meal in slowly while stirring hard to stop lumps.
Keep stirring over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until thick and smooth and it pulls away from the pan. Serve alongside the sauce.

name: fish dish
ingredients: 1 tsp ground spices from the region
Potatoes, rice or bread to serve
steps: Score the fish twice on each side if cooking it whole, so the heat and seasoning reach the middle.
Rub with oil, garlic, spices, salt and lemon and leave 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C or get a griddle hot.
Cook for 12 to 15 minutes a side for a whole fish, or 4 minutes a side for fillets, until the flesh turns opaque and flakes at the thickest point.
Meanwhile soften the onion and tomato in a little oil for 10 minutes for a simple sauce. Serve with the fish and herbs.

name: vegetable dish
ingredients: Rice, bread or potatoes to serve
steps: Cut the vegetables into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.
Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add garlic and spices and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the harder vegetables and the tomatoes and simmer 12 minutes.
Add the softer vegetables and the beans and cook 10 minutes more until everything is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Season, finish with herbs and serve with rice, bread or potatoes.
